fixes.explanation: No root, that's the reason. Jesus says, “But when the sun rose, the seedlings were scorched, and they withered because they had no root.” The seed sprang up quickly, but nothing was holding it below. I know the feeling of looking sharp and being shaky underneath, friend.

The boat is where Jesus sat in verse 1, but verse 10 says they asked Him about the parable. When Jesus is alone with the Twelve and those around Him, the parable is the topic. A boat makes a fine seat, but it's not the question the text gives.

Verse 11: “The mystery of the kingdom of God has been given to you…” That's what Jesus says to the Twelve and those around Him. Then comes the other side, that to those on the outside everything is expressed in parables. I know what it's like to be handed something I never expected, like a whole bakery after years in a junk drawer.
Satan comes and takes the word away. Jesus says, “As soon as they hear it, Satan comes and takes away the word that was sown in them.” Notice the words “As soon as…” That is quick work.
Nobody argues in this verse. Jesus says that as soon as they hear it, Satan comes and takes away the word that was sown in them. It's Satan doing the taking, not a debate.

Forgetting by morning is a very human guess, and I've forgotten plenty before breakfast. But Jesus says Satan comes “As soon as they hear it…” and takes away the word. So the verse names who does the taking.

Studying and teaching others isn't what verse 20 says. It says they “…hear the word, receive it, and produce a crop…” I'd happily study alongside you, friend, but those three are the ones Jesus names.
False is right. The verse says the seed sprouts and grows “…though he knows not how.” The man sleeps and wakes, and the seed keeps going. I bet that man sleeps better than I do.
It's actually true, friend. Verse 28 says, “All by itself the earth produces a crop…” The man scatters the seed, and the earth does the producing.
A staff is a fine walking stick, but Jesus names a sickle. The man swings it as soon as the grain is ripe, because the harvest has come. Nobody's harvesting grain with a walking stick, friend.

More parables is a fair guess, since this chapter is full of them. But the verse says privately He explained everything to His own disciples. Explaining is what He does privately with His own disciples.
